Hi Liam / Priya,

Thanks again for the conversation this week — really appreciate the clarity on expected throughput growth for Q1. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concrete proposal on the table so Procurement and Finance have something to review:

Proposal summary (high level)
- Move Archon to Premium SLA (24/7 priority oncall, 15 min P1 response, monthly latency SLO 99th pct < 220ms)
- Increase committed capacity by 2x (baseline tokens/month), with a 3-month burst buffer layered on top for onboarding spikes
- One-time credit to offset migration cost: 10% credit applied to the first three invoices after amendment
- Term: 12-month amendment that rolls existing contract forward; includes an opt-out at renewal if throughput is below threshold

Attachments: Proposed-SLA-Amendment-v3.pdf (pdf), Capacity-Reservation-Appendix.xlsx (xlsx)

As next steps, can you confirm the following by EOD Monday?
1) Whether Procurement wants the credit applied as an invoice line item or as a prepaid credit balance
2) Any mandatory legal redlines your team needs us to feed to Legal for a final SLA schedule
3) Target signature date — suggested: Nov 30 to have changes effective Dec 1

If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute call with Marissa (our Head of Customer Ops) to walk through the latency targets and escalation paths.

Thanks,

- Can you confirm the monthly delta in list price (per-token) for the Premium SLA vs our current plan? We need a clear delta to run through our cost models.
- For the 3-month burst buffer, is that "free" capacity (i.e., won't be billed if not used) or billed at a discounted overage rate?

Procurement asked me to loop in their billing contact (procurement@archon.ai) because they'll need the final schedule for PO amendment and internal approvals.

We can target Nov 30 for signature, but Procurement will likely request a one-week review period after Legal sees the SLA schedule.
